proofs.requirement: A changed recycling, damage or death process does not by itself establish a survival requirement in the relevant cells.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Cancer cells can change how they manage damage, recycling and death. A changed process is not automatically a survival requirement. Experiments must test what the relevant cells need under the stated conditions.

proofs.requirement: Explain the tested NBR1/MHC-I route, immune-dependence interventions and the chloroquine monotherapy limitation in the linked canonical record.
proofs.claimType: Targeted primary-body verification with defined cell and mouse systems.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Yamamoto and colleagues found that the cargo receptor NBR1 helped direct MHC-I proteins to lysosomes through an autophagy-dependent route in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma models. This lowered the amount of MHC-I at the cell surface, where it displays antigens to CD8 T cells. In mouse experiments, reducing MHC-I or depleting CD8 T cells reversed tumour control after genetic autophagy inhibition. Chloroquine increased surface MHC-I but, alone, did not significantly reduce tumour weight in the reported experiment; its effects on lysosomes are broad. These model results do not establish that every KRAS-driven cancer depends on autophagy or that blocking it benefits patients.
